rule: An unresolved conflict blocks promotion of the stronger dependent claim. Engineering sources remain authoritative for resolution; the language system records impact and release controls.

conflicts.summary: Resolved: STATUS.md previously asserted both a wired ModelCanvas with shared selection and a 3D stack with zero consumers. The run-model-canvas-capability-check.mjs browser check proved the 3D tab reachable, rendering through WebGL2, with bidirectional plan-shared selection; STATUS.md now records the verified viewing-surface truth.
conflicts.downstreamRule: Do not market or answer disputed 3D reachability as settled.

conflicts.summary: The tier overlap is decided and the read half is proven; the write half is neither. ADR-0028 (accepted 2026-08-04) gives canonical local working state to SQLite in an ARQ-owned Worker over OPFS and bounds IndexedDB to recovery bridging and replaceable caches, and ADR-0030 records the working-copy and recovery tiers. Opening a portable file into that working copy is browser-verified. Nothing checkpoints the working copy back out to a portable .arq file, so portable-arq-publication still has no tested write flow. This is no longer an undecided architecture question; it is a missing implementation with missing evidence, and it stays blocking until both exist.
conflicts.downstreamRule: Name the concrete persistence tier. Neither a journal append nor an opened working copy implies portable-file publication.

requires: A tested write flow that checkpoints the working copy back to a portable .arq file.
Reopen-after-write evidence proving the written file is a complete, sidecar-free project.
Status and message adapters updated for the write and publication states.
satisfied: An ADR resolving the persistence relationship: ADR-0028 accepted 2026-08-04, ADR-0030 accepted.
The read half of the open/write flow: benchmarks/results/native-open-capability-2026-08-11T07-34-26-854Z.json.

conflicts.summary: Resolved, and in the opposite direction to the one first recorded. The drift began as public copy promising an open the product could not do; it ended as public copy denying an open the product had shipped. The file panel no longer stops at compatibility preflight: it copies the chosen file into a project-scoped OPFS working copy in an ARQ-owned Worker and adopts the project into the workspace. The public pages now say that, and they carry the limit with it - opening is current, writing back to the chosen file is not - asserted by rendered tests rather than left to prose.
conflicts.downstreamRule: State the open and its limit in the same breath: the chosen file is not written to. A described open never implies portable-arq-publication.

requires: Promote only after a browser opening-path test.
